en.name: Split peas, dried
en.summary: Dried split peas keep about 1 year from purchase, and about 1 year again from the day the bag is opened if they go straight into a sealed jar. Like other pulses they harden with age rather than spoiling, which shows up as soup that never quite goes smooth.
en.pantry: An airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard gives about 1 year from purchase and about 1 year from opening. Splitting the pea removes the skin and exposes the whole inner surface, so split peas take up damp and stale a little faster than whole dried peas do — worth knowing if you are choosing between them for long storage. Light fades the colour, particularly in green split peas, and pantry weevils are the fast problem. Old split peas need longer simmering and sometimes never break down into the purée that is the point of pea soup.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for split peas, so none is given here, and a dry cupboard already covers a year. In a hot, humid kitchen an airtight jar in the fridge is a reasonable precaution against damp and insects — bring it back to room temperature before opening so condensation forms on the jar rather than on the peas. Cooked split peas and pea soup are a different food: cool them quickly in shallow containers and refrigerate covered.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for dried split peas. Freezing a sealed bag for a few days deals with insect eggs in a bulk purchase, which is genuinely useful, but it is a pest measure and not a shelf life, and it does nothing about age-hardening. Cooked pea soup freezes extremely well and is the better use of the space.
spoilage: Live weevils, small moths, webbing or fine dust in the jar.
A musty or mouldy smell, meaning damp has got in.
Peas that stay gritty and firm after a long simmer.
Colour faded to a dull grey-beige, which is a quality change rather than a safety one.
tips: Decant into an airtight jar and date the lid on the day you buy them.
Rinse and pick over before cooking; grit and small stones are common.
Buy whole dried peas instead if you are storing for a long time.
Freeze the finished soup rather than hoarding dry peas you will not cook.

faq.q: How long do dried split peas keep?
faq.a: About 1 year from purchase, and about 1 year from opening in an airtight jar.
Not usually — they are split and skinless, so they cook down without a soak. Old ones simply need longer simmering.

faq.q: Why will my split peas not go soft?
faq.a: Age. Pulses harden in storage, and old split peas may never break down into a smooth purée however long you cook them.

zh.name: 乾豌豆瓣
zh.summary: 乾豌豆瓣從購買日起算約可放 1 年；只要一開封就換裝密封罐，開封後同樣約 1 年。和其他豆類一樣，它的結局是隨年紀變硬而不是腐敗，表現出來就是那鍋濃湯怎麼煮都不夠綿。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算約 1 年，開封後約 1 年。剖半去皮把整個內部表面都露出來，所以豌豆瓣吸濕和走味都比整顆乾豌豆快一點——如果你在考慮長期儲存要買哪一種，這點值得知道。光線會讓顏色變淡，青豌豆瓣尤其明顯，而櫥櫃裡的米象則是來得最快的問題。放久的豌豆瓣要煮更久，有時甚至煮不成那鍋濃湯該有的綿密質地。
zh.fridge: 乾豌豆瓣沒有公布的冷藏期限，本頁也不給，而乾燥櫥櫃本來就有一年。濕熱的廚房裡，密封罐放冰箱是防潮防蟲的合理措施——開封前先回到室溫，讓水氣凝在罐子上而不是豆子上。煮熟的豌豆瓣和豌豆濃湯則是另一種食物：請用淺容器快速降溫並加蓋冷藏。
zh.freezer: 乾豌豆瓣沒有給冷凍數字。把密封袋冷凍幾天可以解決大量採購的蟲卵問題，這確實有用，但那是防蟲措施不是保存期限，而且對「變硬」毫無幫助。煮好的豌豆湯非常耐凍，把冷凍庫空間留給它更划算。
spoilage: 罐內出現活的米象、小蛾、絲網或細粉屑。
聞到潮霉味，代表濕氣跑進去了。
煮很久之後還是沙沙的、硬硬的。
顏色褪成暗淡的灰米色——這是品質變化，不是安全問題。
tips: 買回來當天倒進密封罐，並在蓋子上寫日期。
煮之前先挑再洗；混入砂石很常見。
要長期存放的話，改買整顆乾豌豆。
與其囤著不會煮的乾豆，不如把煮好的湯冷凍起來。

faq.a: 從購買日起算約 1 年；開封後放密封罐也是約 1 年。
通常不用——它已經剖半去皮，不泡也煮得開。放久的只是要煮更久。

faq.q: 為什麼我的豌豆瓣煮不爛？
faq.a: 因為放太久。豆類在保存中會變硬，老的豌豆瓣不管煮多久，都可能煮不成綿密的泥。
